mechanism: Imagine Trays → Sort Facts → Balance Verdict
title: THE TWO-TRAY TEST
goal: A loud conclusion still has to pass inspection.
steps: 1. Imagine Trays — Imagine two trays.
2. Name Sides — Name the left SUPPORTS IT and the right DOESN’T FIT.
3. Sort Facts — Drop only visible facts into them—no feelings disguised as evidence.
4. Switch Sides — Now cover the fuller tray and read the neglected one silently.
5. Balance Verdict — Finish with a verdict that can hold both sides without pretending they weigh the same.
win: ✓ Both trays stayed visible; the verdict stopped being one-sided.
tips: Keep clarity in sight when a strong feeling narrows attention.
Choose a grounded choice when the mind asks for immediate relief.
Use a wider view before turning emotional weather into a life rule.
Before reacting to a strong feeling, ask what protects perspective.
Your attention is valuable; do not spend it all on emotional weather.

mechanism: Name Fear → Add Likely → Act Now
title: WORST CASE, WITH EXITS
goal: A worst-case story loses size when it gains a route.
steps: 1. Name Fear — Picture the feared ending in one line.
2. Build Exits — Under it build four rungs: WHAT HAPPENS; WHAT I DO NEXT; WHO OR WHAT HELPS; HOW RECOVERY COULD BEGIN.
3. Add Likely — Add a fifth rung for the outcome that is actually most likely.
4. Climb Route — Move through the five steps once in your mind.
5. Act Now — Then take the first coping action available now.
win: ✓ The forecast lost its monopoly.
tips: Keep responsibility proportionate when catastrophic thinking gets personal.
Let one coping option make room for a different outcome.
Your mind can be protective and still misread catastrophic thinking.
Choose what supports realism, not what feeds worst-case living.
Catastrophic thinking may need patience more than another explanation.

mechanism: Score Odds → Weigh Evidence → Follow Evidence
title: THE ODDS RECEIPT
goal: Fear speaks in certainty; reality keeps percentages.
steps: 1. Score Odds — Give the prediction a number from 0 to 100.
2. Check Baseline — Find one real reference point: how often has this happened in similar situations?
3. Weigh Evidence — Notice one fact that raises the odds and another that lowers them.
4. Revise Odds — Pick a new number and remember it.
5. Follow Evidence — Act from the revision, not the original alarm.
win: ✓ Disaster stopped being the only ending.
tips: You do not have to solve the worst-case forecast at its loudest.
Pause fear forecasting; give the next practical step a fair chance.
Do not let certainty inflation turn discomfort into a command.
Keep the next move connected to perspective.
Choose actual probabilities while worst-case living is still only an option.
mindBend: Certainty is a feeling your mind can produce. Fear speaks in certainty; reality keeps percentages
formulaFlow: Score Odds → Check Baseline → Weigh Evidence → Revise Odds → Follow Evidence
safety:

This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

mechanism: Imagine A Pie → Check The Whole → Choose Repair
title: THE BLAME PIE
goal: Owning your part is different from taking all the blame.
steps: 1. Imagine A Pie — Imagine a pie that stands for everything that caused the situation.
2. Share The Slices — In your mind, give slices to your choices, other people, circumstances, systems, timing, and chance.
3. Check The Whole — Make sure all slices together equal 100.
4. Find Your Slice — Focus only on your true share.
5. Choose Repair — Picture one repair for your slice. Let the rest stay outside your responsibility.
win: ✓ My slice stayed mine; the rest went back to the whole pie.
tips: Give self-compassion enough time to change the next moment.
Choose growth first, then decide what self-blame needs.
Choose self-compassion before deciding what self-blame means.
Give self-compassion more authority than self-punishment.
Guilt does not cancel your access to self-respect.
mindBend: Notice the difference between what your mind predicts and what the moment proves. Owning your part is different from taking all the blame

safety:

mechanism: Name Extremes → Place Today → Choose Response
title: THE GREY DIAL
goal: Binary thinking hates a numbered dial.
steps: 1. Name Extremes — Name the two extremes your mind is using.
2. Build Scale — Build a 0–10 scale between them and say three real anchor points: 2, 5, and 8.
3. Place Today — Place today’s event where the evidence fits—not where the emotion shouts.
4. Choose Response — Choose a response matched to that exact setting.
win: ✓ The dial found a middle, and the response found its size.
tips: Choose a wider view before deciding that a fixed story will last.
Keep choice closer than the urge toward rigid certainty.
Choose a wider view; your mind can update later.

mechanism: Keep Event → Predict Different → Speak Plurals
title: THREE WORLDS, ONE FACT
goal: One fact can support more than one world.
steps: 1. Keep Event — Keep the event fixed.
2. Invent — Invent three models for why it happened.
3. Predict Different — Each model must predict a different thing you could observe next.
4. Earliest — Notice the earliest observation that would separate them.
5. Speak Plurals — Until that evidence arrives, speak in plurals: possibilities, not prophecy.
win: ✓ Possibilities plural. Prophecy cancelled.
tips: One pause can protect confidence from worst-case living.
Choose the likely outcome; you can reassess after a disaster prediction softens.
Let the worst-case forecast remain unfinished while you choose the likely outcome.
Give facts room to challenge catastrophic thinking.
Choose one coping option and leave the bigger judgement for later.

One fact can support more than one world.

win_reward: ✓ The word lost its spell; I heard sound without obeying meaning.
fullRitual:
WORD MELT

GOAL
Repeat the sound until the spell loses its language.

1. Choose Charged — Choose one charged word—not a whole painful story.
2. Say Gently — Say it gently and steadily for about twenty seconds.
3. Listen Moment — Listen for the moment it becomes rhythm, mouth movement, or noise.
4. Stop Room — Stop there and look around the room.
5. Return Seen — Meaning may return; you have seen it separate once.

WIN
✓ The word lost its spell; I heard sound without obeying meaning.

TIPS
• Let more control guide the response, even with automatic behaviour present.
• Autopilot can change shape when pressure drops.
• Do not confuse automatic behaviour with a permanent verdict.
• You can honour automatic behaviour and still refuse autopilot.
• Take autopilot seriously without treating it as destiny.

MIND BEND
The first story arrived first, not necessarily best. Repeat the sound until the spell loses its language

FORMULA FLOW
Choose Charged → Say Gently → Listen Moment → Stop Room → Return Seen

SAFETY
PAUSE
Avoid this with slurs, trauma phrases, voices, or material that escalates symptoms.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: THE BAD VOICE ACTOR
goal: Authority often hides inside delivery.
steps: 1. Read Wrong — Hear the thought as a tired GPS, an overdramatic sports commentator, or a hesitant intern reading the wrong memo.
2. Keep Words — Keep the words unchanged; alter only tempo, pitch, and confidence.
3. Replay — Then replay it in your natural voice as a possibility, not an order.

tips: Keep responsibility proportionate when rigid certainty gets personal.
Protect mental flexibility; rigid certainty does not need every answer.
Let one fresh question make the situation easier to carry.
Let a more flexible interpretation create a little distance from rigid certainty.
Make room for a wider view instead of feeding rigid certainty.

goal: Give thought transport, not a throne.
steps: 1. Place Thought — Place the thought on something imagined as moving: a bus, leaf, or subtitle.

4. Allow Departure — Another carrier may come; none owns the station.

mechanism: Set Code → Reverse Code → Claim Control
title: PLAY THE BODY PASSWORD
goal: A short body code can prove that alarm has not taken every control.
steps: 1. Set Code — Choose three tiny comfortable movements, such as tap a knee, touch a thumb, and shift your gaze.

4. Claim Control — Name the movement you directed most clearly, then let the code stop.

win_reward: ✓ Panic became a wave with surroundings around it.
fullRitual:
BURN THE EXCESS CHARGE

GOAL
Give body alarm a finish line.

1. Choose Burst — Choose a safe vigorous movement you can do comfortably.
2. Count Ten — Do ten controlled repetitions without chasing exhaustion.
3. End Completely — Stop, feel the after-pulse, and let breathing settle naturally.
4. Let Body — Let the body spend energy without spending your future.

WIN
✓ Panic became a wave with surroundings around it.

TIPS
• Let settling have more influence than escape rushing today.
• Let a surge of fear be temporary, even when the issue is real.
• Let safety cues survive the pull toward catastrophe checking.
• Panic can feel convincing before the evidence agrees.
• Use present-moment facts to protect what matters after a racing sensation passes.

MIND BEND
Certainty is a feeling your mind can produce. Give body alarm a finish line

FORMULA FLOW
Choose Burst → Set Short → End Completely → Let Body

SAFETY
PAUSE
Do not attempt intense movement with injury, illness, pregnancy concerns, or medical restrictions.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

mechanism: Breathe Pulling → Repeat Comfortable → Breathe Workable

goal: Make urgency leave through a gentler exit.
steps: 1. Breathe Pulling — Breathe in without pulling extra air.

4. Breathe Workable — After several rounds, resume natural breathing and look for one workable decision.

fullRitual:
DATE-STAMP THE PRESENT

GOAL
Give the body proof that time has moved.

1. Say Now — Say the full date, your current age, location, and who is here.
2. Name Differences — Name three differences between now and the remembered danger.
3. Mark Present — Name one visible or audible fact that belongs only to today.

WIN
✓ The mind returned from elsewhere without needing a perfect landing.

TIPS
• Do not abandon present safety just because the old danger signal is loud.
• Let distance be the measure, not flooding through.
• Keep present safety protected while a memory surge finds its level.
• Let the past feeling close settle before creating a permanent conclusion.
• Keep a painful memory honest by checking what memory forcing adds.

MIND BEND
Your mind can say “give the body proof that time has moved” and still leave room for a different next move.

Say Age → Name Differences → State Belongs

SAFETY
PAUSE
Use immediate professional help if you cannot regain sense of where you are or safety.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

mechanism: Read Channels → Move Dial → Check Panel
title: DISASSEMBLE THE ALARM PANEL
goal: The whole alarm does not need to stop before one dial can move.
steps: 1. Read Channels — Read three channels without searching your whole body: SPEED, PRESSURE, and TEMPERATURE. Use lower, medium, or high.

3. Move Dial — Move only that channel one step: slow one hand movement, soften one contact point, or adjust one safe layer of warmth or coolness.
4. Check Panel — Check whether that channel changed at all. Let the other two channels remain exactly as they are.

mechanism: Seat Feelings → Clear Board → Choose Survivor

win_reward: ✓ A sound appeared before its label could grab it.
fullRitual:
THE MILLISECOND BEFORE THE NAME

GOAL
What you notice exists briefly before concept files it.

1. Look Touch — Look at or touch something ordinary.
2. Catch Bare — Catch the first bare instant before ‘cup,’ ‘cold,’ ownership, or preference appears.
3. Don't Freeze — Do not freeze it; simply recognise the order: contact, then concept.
4. Repeat Unnamed — Repeat with a sound.

WIN
✓ A sound appeared before its label could grab it.

TIPS
• Use the observing perspective to stay connected with freedom.
• Keep the thought stream honest by checking what identity fusion adds.
• Let mental space be the measure, not observer loss.
• When a sticky thought rises, return to one step back.
• Give room around the thought more authority than mental arguing.

MIND BEND
What feels automatic can still be interrupted. What you notice exists briefly before concept files it

FORMULA FLOW
Look Touch → Catch Bare → Don't Freeze → Repeat Unnamed

SAFETY
PAUSE
End if preidea-based attention feels unreal or confusing.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

mechanism: Name Stack → Check Remainder → Rebuild Stack
title: PLAY EMOTION JENGA
goal: Pull one feeling from the stack and see what is actually holding.
steps: 1. Name Stack — Name two or three feelings and place each on a separate mental block.
2. Pull One — Temporarily bracket one block with the phrase ‘not deleted—just outside this test.’
3. Check Remainder — Observe what changes in the remainder: body location, urge, story, intensity, or nothing at all. Keep one difference.
4. Rebuild Stack — Restore the removed block. Repeat only if useful, then rebuild the complete stack before finishing.
win: ✓ The emotional stack revealed which block was actually carrying the weight.
tips: Do not use urge feeding as proof that an impulse is correct.
Keep self-control in sight when the urge narrows attention.
Take one safer choice seriously when the urge feels overwhelming.
The urge is real; craving escalation is still optional.
Let self-control have more influence than impulse obedience today.

fullRitual:
THE HONEST DOOR

GOAL
Replace time pressure with one concrete time decision.

1. Name the Window — Decide whether this is a now task, today task, or later task.
2. Estimate Once — Give it one rough duration without repeatedly recalculating.
3. Choose Start — Name the next real start point.
4. Act or Park — Begin now or deliberately park it until that start point.

WIN
✓ Time became a decision instead of a vague source of pressure.

TIPS
• A clean re-entry is a real executive skill when freezing when the first step is unclear.
• Let one honest fact carry more weight than mental noise during entry ambiguity.
• Compassion is compatible with clear limits and real responsibility while entry ambiguity is active.
• Let the next action serve your values rather than your loudest impulse in this entry ambiguity moment.
• If this only partly helps, follow the part that is still loud after freezing when the first step is unclear.

MIND BEND
A deadline feels less magical when it is translated into a start. This moment—freezing when the first step is unclear—still leaves a next move.

FORMULA FLOW
Window → Estimate → Start → Act/Park

SAFETY
PAUSE
Stop if the exercise increases agitation or if the task involves immediate safety, medical, legal, or emergency decisions requiring qualified help.

fullRitual:
THE HONEST DEADLINE

GOAL
Turn a crowded plan into one ranked decision.

1. List Three — Hold only the three most important demands in mind.
2. Choose Cost — Ask which one becomes more expensive if ignored today.
3. Name First — Choose the first action inside that priority.
4. Protect It — Let the other two remain intentionally undone for this round.

WIN
✓ Competing demands became one chosen direction.

TIPS
• One visible priority can quiet several invisible ones when losing track of time while working in the moment.
• Let one honest fact carry more weight than mental noise during time drift.
• Compassion is compatible with clear limits and real responsibility while time drift is active.
• Let the next action serve your values rather than your loudest impulse in this time drift moment.
• If this only partly helps, follow the part that is still loud after losing track of time while working in the moment.

MIND BEND
Prioritising is not choosing what matters forever; it is choosing what leads now. This moment—losing track of time while working in the moment—still leaves a next move.

fullRitual:
THE HONEST NO

GOAL
Enter the social moment without waiting to feel completely comfortable.

1. Find Anchor — Notice one person, topic, or shared context you can genuinely respond to.
2. Small Entry — Use one simple observation or question.
3. Stay Curious — Ask one follow-up instead of monitoring how you are performing.
4. Exit Cleanly — When needed, leave with a simple closing rather than disappearing.

WIN
✓ You joined the moment without requiring perfect social confidence.

TIPS
• Listening accurately is different from agreeing when agreeing to something you resent in the moment.
• Let one honest fact carry more weight than mental noise during compliance reflex.
• Compassion is compatible with clear limits and real responsibility while compliance reflex is active.
• Let the next action serve your values rather than your loudest impulse in this compliance reflex moment.
• If this only partly helps, follow the part that is still loud after agreeing to something you resent in the moment.

MIND BEND

THE SIMPLE TRUST

GOAL
Reduce the performance to the first controllable cue.

1. Feet — Feel the floor or chair supporting you.
2. First Line — Name only the first sentence or first action.
3. Pace — Slow the first ten seconds by one degree.

GOAL
Separate what is urgent from what is actually meaningful.

1. Zoom Out — Picture this week from one year away.
2. Name Value — Name the value you want this decision or season to express.
3. Remove Audience — Imagine nobody could applaud or criticise the choice.
4. Choose Signal — Name one action that would still matter.

WIN
✓ Meaning became a direction instead of a vague feeling.

TIPS
• Meaning can guide action without answering everything when you are busy but unsure what the effort is for.
• Do not demand certainty from a moment that cannot provide it during purpose drift.
• Your attention is valuable, so spend it deliberately while purpose drift is active.
• Notice what the situation proves before adding what it might mean in this purpose drift moment.
• If this only partly helps, follow the part that is still loud after you are busy but unsure what the effort is for.

MIND BEND
A goal can be impressive and still not be yours. This moment—you are busy but unsure what the effort is for—still leaves a next move.

FORMULA FLOW
Zoom Out → Value → Remove Audience → Choose

SAFETY
PAUSE
Spiritual or meaning reflection should not replace medical or mental-health care, and should not be used to explain away abuse, danger, severe symptoms, or urgent practical needs.

2. Add Distance — Place 'I notice my mind saying…' before it.
3. Find Now — Name one fact in the present that the sentence does not contain.
4. Choose — Act from the present fact rather than the sentence alone.

WIN
✓ The thought became one sentence inside a larger moment.

TIPS
• Mental repetition is not the same as new evidence when you are treating mental content like an instruction.
• Use the next minute as the size of the problem for now during thought-command fusion.
• A useful pause is action when the alternative is automatic reaction while thought-command fusion is active.
• Give your nervous system and your judgement different jobs in this thought-command fusion moment.
• If this only partly helps, follow the part that is still loud after you are treating mental content like an instruction.

MIND BEND
A sentence in your head can feel like a room; it is still a sentence. This moment—you are treating mental content like an instruction—still leaves a next move.

FORMULA FLOW
Quote → Distance → Now → Choose

SAFETY
PAUSE
Stop if the exercise increases disorientation, trauma flooding, compulsive checking, or severe distress. Seek appropriate professional support when symptoms are persistent, intense, or unsafe.
